chain.label: Mountain-wave-driven strong, gusty westerly crosswind at DEN
chain.trigger: mountain wave and downsloping wind conditions existed... resulted in strong westerly winds and very localized, intermittent wind gusts as high as 45 knots

chain.label: ATCT local controller issued only lower runway departure-end wind (27 kt), not the more adverse airport wind (35 kt gusting 40 kt)
chain.trigger: the DEN ATCT local controller did not provide the accident pilots with any additional wind information... the pilots were not aware of the high winds that they would encounter during the takeoff roll

chain.label: Continental's 737-500 simulators could not model gusty winds below 50 feet agl
chain.trigger: its FFS atmospheric model software allowed for only steady state wind inputs—no gusting winds—below 50 feet agl

chain.label: Captain's crosswind training never exposed him to realistic gusty crosswind dynamics
chain.trigger: the captain was not adequately prepared to respond to the changes in heading encountered during this takeoff

caused_by.evidence: Continental's simulator training did not replicate the ground-level disturbances and gusting crosswinds that often occur at or near the runway surface

chain.label: Airplane encountered a strong, rapidly varying wind gust (peak ~45 kt) during the takeoff roll
chain.trigger: A peak gust of 45 knots occurred at 1818:12, about the same time the FDR recorded the right rudder pedal beginning to move aft

caused_by.evidence: a particularly strong wind gust (wind speeds as high as 45 knots) moved across the center of the airport, directly crossing the airplane's path around the time of the accident takeoff
if the accident pilots had been advised of the existing AW... it is likely that they would have reconsidered their departure on that runway

chain.label: Captain ceased/relaxed right rudder pedal input as the nose swung rapidly left, instead of reapplying rudder
chain.trigger: the captain abruptly relaxed the right pedal to its neutral position... the captain stopped making rudder pedal inputs entirely

caused_by.evidence: This strong crosswind gust increased the airplane's sideslip angle, significantly reduced the effect of the captain's 72-percent rudder pedal input, and weathervaned the airplane's nose further to the left
the airplane encountered a strong and gusty crosswind that exceeded the captain's training and experience

chain.label: Airplane's nose swung rapidly and uncontrollably left of the runway centerline
chain.trigger: the airplane's heading continued to move left of the baseline heading at an increasing rate

caused_by.evidence: instead of making another significant right rudder pedal input (the only control input that could have corrected the airplane's leftward veer off the runway), the captain began to make disorganized and ineffective control inputs

chain.label: Captain applied ineffective right control wheel and nosewheel steering tiller inputs instead of rudder correction
chain.trigger: he began to apply right control wheel (aileron) inputs... and he tried to steer the airplane to the right using the nosewheel steering tiller

caused_by.evidence: the captain's use of tiller and full right control wheel in the 3 seconds before the excursion likely resulted from acute stress stemming from a sudden, unexpected threat, perceived lack of control, and extreme time pressure

chain.label: Airplane departed the left side of runway 34R
chain.trigger: the accident airplane departed the left side of runway 34R about 2,600 feet from the approach end and crossed taxiway WC and an airport service road

caused_by.evidence: the airplane continued off the runway
neither input had a significant effect on the airplane's heading

chain.label: Captain's initiation of the rejected takeoff was delayed several seconds
chain.trigger: the captain's initiation of a rejected takeoff was delayed by about 2 to 4 seconds because he was occupied with the nosewheel steering tiller and right control wheel input

caused_by.evidence: the captain did not have his right hand on the thrust levers during the excursion... the need to reposition his right hand to the thrust levers as the airplane was bouncing along uneven ground also likely contributed to the delay

chain.label: Cockpit seats certified only to older static load standard, not modern 16-G dynamic crashworthiness standard
chain.trigger: the cockpit seats in the accident airplane were designed to meet the structural requirements of 14 CFR 25.561... [and were] not required to meet those [16-G dynamic] crashworthiness standards

chain.label: Captain and passengers seriously/minorly injured; airplane substantially damaged in impact and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: The captain and 5 of the 110 passengers were seriously injured; the first officer, 2 cabin crewmembers, and 38 passengers received minor injuries... The airplane was substantially damaged

caused_by.evidence: as the airplane crossed the uneven terrain before coming to a stop, it became airborne, resulting in a jarring impact when it regained contact with the ground
the captain's actions during his final attempts to keep the airplane on the runway... also delayed him from performing a rejected takeoff
the accident pilots' injuries would have likely been lessened or eliminated if their seats had been designed to meet the crashworthiness requirements of 14 CFR 25.562
